# rand.generator

A source of random numbers, as `rand.generator(seed)` and `os.rand_generator()` answer it.

## Overview

`rand.generator` is owned by the [`rand`](../stdlib/rand.md) module. It is ONE type over two sources, so anything
that takes a generator — `array.shuffle(g)`, a function of your own — accepts either:

| constructor | source | sequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rand.generator(seed)` (pure) | PCG-DXSM, seeded | the same for the same seed, on every build |
| `os.rand_generator()` (needs the `os` grant) | `crypto/rand` | unpredictable |

Every draw is derived from the source's raw 64-bit output by Kavun's own code (bounded ints without bias, 53-bit
floats, Box–Muller normals, Fisher–Yates permutations), so a seeded sequence depends only on PCG-DXSM — a specified
algorithm — and not on Go's library helpers. A draw moves the generator's state: it is the value's own, never shared
with another script.

```go
g := import("rand").generator(1)
g.draw_int(100)             // => 59 — then 8, then 71: seed 1 always starts this way
g.draw_int(1, 7)            // a die roll in [1, 7)
g.draw_float()              // [0, 1)
g.draw_perm(4)              // a permutation of 0…3
d := import("os").rand_generator()
d.draw_int(1, 7)            // unpredictable
```

## Operators

| operator | reading |
| --- | --- |
| `==` / `!=` | the same generator (identity — two generators with the same seed are still two) |
| `!` | a generator is always truthy |
| everything else | raises |

## Ranges

Ranges are half-open, like `range(lo, hi)`.

## Render

The render names the source, not a constructor expression — no expression rebuilds a state mid-sequence. There is
no `string()`.

<a id="array"></a>
### `array([default]) -> array`

Answer a new one-element `array` holding the receiver.

Total, so the default is never used.

```go
import("rand").generator(1).array().len()   // => 1
```

<a id="copy"></a>
### `copy() -> rand.generator`

Answer an independent clone at the same state for a seeded generator; an entropy generator answers itself.

The seeded clone and the original then draw the same sequence.

<a id="draw_bytes"></a>
### `draw_bytes(n) -> bytes`

Draw `n` random octets (`1 ≤ n ≤` the sequence ceiling).

<a id="draw_exp"></a>
### `draw_exp() -> float`

Draw from the exponential distribution (rate 1).

<a id="draw_float"></a>
### `draw_float() -> float` / `draw_float(hi) -> float` / `draw_float(lo, hi) -> float`

Draw a float in [0, 1), [0, hi) or [lo, hi); bounds must be finite and non-empty.

<a id="draw_int"></a>
### `draw_int() -> int` / `draw_int(hi) -> int` / `draw_int(lo, hi) -> int`

Draw an int in [0, 2^63), [0, hi) or [lo, hi); an empty range raises `invalid_value`.

<a id="draw_norm"></a>
### `draw_norm() -> float`

Draw from the standard normal distribution (mean 0, deviation 1).

<a id="draw_perm"></a>
### `draw_perm(n) -> array`

Draw a random permutation of `0…n-1`.

<a id="format"></a>
### `format([spec]) -> string`

Render the generator by its source: `<rand.generator:seeded>` or `<rand.generator:entropy>`.

<a id="freeze"></a>
### `freeze() -> rand.generator`

Answer the generator itself.

<a id="is_true"></a>
### `is_true() -> bool`

Report truthiness: a generator is always truthy.
